messages:
maya: Heads-up — the insights widget in the console showed metrics for a different workspace after I switched orgs quickly. Repro: 1) open workspace A, 2) open Insights, 3) Cmd-K to jump to workspace B, 4) panel still showed A's active sessions for ~3s.
kevin: ugh. Can you grab the network trace / props passed to the widget?
maya: attaching snippet of console logs: 
`GET /api/insights/snippet?widgetId=42&env=prod 200 { cacheKey: 'widget:42:user:987' }`
lucy: that cacheKey looks wrong — it's keyed only on user, not workspace. If you switch workspace we hydrate from user-scoped cache before route renders.
jordan: so race between route change and widget hydration. If server-side prefetch returns quickly, frontend mounts with stale state.
ashley: does this flow happen for both hosted and private customers? curious for Dedicated customers with per-tenant quotas.
maya: reprod on hosted and dedicated in my local repro (using a prod snapshot).
kevin: quick mitigation: invalidate widget cache on route switch. Longer term we should include workspaceId in cache key and add a server-side guard to avoid returning cross-workspace data.
lucy: agreed. Proposed cache key change: `widget:${id}:user:${uid}:ws:${workspaceId}` and bump cache version. Add unit tests for hydrateOnMount when route param changes.
jordan: also want telemetry covered — telemetry events currently log workspaceId in payload sometimes via route metadata, sometimes via the user session. Mixing strategies made this tricky to audit. We should standardize to always source workspaceId from the route context for UI events, and include trace_id for correlation.
kevin: internal-api debate: do we require every insights endpoint to take explicit x-workspace-id header and soft-assert on server? I prefer explicit header + server-side assertion: if header != session.active_workspace -> log warning + 403 (or 409?).
lucy: I think 403 on mismatch could break legitimate proxy flows (console server acting on behalf of user). Maybe 409 + telemetry event is safer while we roll out checks.
ashley: from quota perspective, returning another workspace's data could misattribute usage/insights. If we fail closed (403) customers might see missing tiles. Prefer fail open with audit logs for first rollout.
jordan: plan: (1) frontend cache key change + invalidation on route change (fast rollout), (2) backend endpoint soft-assert that logs events when header/session mismatch (ff gated), (3) add a nightly job to scan traces for cross-workspace reads.
maya: I'll push a small frontend PR with cache bump and explicit invalidation. Will add a short e2e that simulates rapid switch.
kevin: sample middleware we can ship behind ff: 
```js
function workspaceGuard(req, res, next) {
  const header = req.header('x-workspace-id');
  const sessionWs = req.session && req.session.activeWorkspace;
  if (header && sessionWs && header !== sessionWs) {
    // soft-assert for now
    log.warn('workspace-mismatch', { header, sessionWs, path: req.path });
    // attach trace tag and continue
    req.trace('workspace_mismatch', { header, sessionWs });
  }
  next();
}
```
lucy: tests to add: unit for cache key, integration for route-switch timing, and a telemetry test that simulated header mismatch increments a metric.
ashley: action on quotas: we should mark tenant-specific quota de-dupe codepath and run a smoke test — I'll own that CI check.
jordan: UX/rollouts: console should surface a tiny banner if data might be stale due to fast switching (subtle yellow bar). Helps customers see a short window where tiles are reconciling.
maya: agreed, will tack that into the frontend PR if time.
ops-bot: scheduled deploy window: 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC for frontend quickfix (cache bump).
kevin: i'll open a backend RFC for header policy. Assigning to @lucy for the telemetry part and @ashley for quota smoke.
maya: thanks — I'll post the PR link when ready and add screenshots of the banner. Any objections to the plan? :thumbsup:
